incident-bot: ALERT: Canary health checks failing for release/2025-03-rapid-flip. Error rate spike in eu-west-1: 502s + latency degradation. Trigger: canary latency > 2s and 502+ errors over threshold. Paging: @Alice M @Ben J @Samira R. Severity: SEV-2. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/release-canary-issues
Alice M: On it, joining the canary cluster now.
Ben J: Confirming metrics — p50 jumped to ~2.1s, p95 ~6s for canary traffic starting ~12:34 UTC. Correlation with feature flag flip: feature.fast_path -> ON at 12:33:58.
Samira R: Is this limited to eu-west?
Eng SRE: Looks isolated to eu-west canaries. Global prod lanes are stable. Note: KV cache miss rate for canaries increased 8x, sidecar RPC timeouts rising. :rotating_light:
Carla (PM): Any customer-facing failures reported?
Luis (Support): Support queue: two enterprise customers reported slow / timed-out completions ~15m ago. No orders lost, mostly timeouts on long-running generation requests.
Alice M: I can reproduce locally against canary config. Stack traces show repeated grpc timeouts between runtime and sidecar when quantizer module reload triggers. Example log:
```
2025-05-10T12:34:56.123Z ERROR sidecar: grpc dial timeout to runtime/quantizer (attempt=1)
2025-05-10T12:34:59.456Z WARN runtime: reinitializing quant module, blocking requests
2025-05-10T12:35:01.789Z ERROR http: upstream returned 502 for request id=abcd-1234
```
Ben J: If the sidecar reinit is causing backpressure, we should flip the fast-path flag back off for canaries and let traffic flow the old codepath. Recommend kill-switch first, rollback image next if needed.
Deploy Bot: Runbook step: execute canary kill switch (--scope canary). Authorization ok for Alice M.
Alice M: Executing kill switch now:
```
/fflip set feature.fast_path false --scope canary --actor alice.m --reason "emergency rollback fast_path due to grpc timeouts"
```
Deploy Bot: Acknowledged. Propagating change to canary buckets in eu-west-1 (5 nodes). Delta window ~30s.
Eng SRE: Monitoring: error rate dropping on the first bucket already. Watching p95/p99 and 502 counts. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/xyz/canary-health
Ben J: p95 back down to ~220ms within ~90s, 502s trending back to baseline.
Carla (PM): Good — Luis please prep a short note for the two affected customers explaining mitigation and next steps.
Luis (Support): Sent templated update to both customers. They acknowledged; no escalation requested right now.
Samira R: We should follow up with a rollback of the canary image that introduced the sidecar change and schedule a hotfix. I'll open a PR to revert the runtime-sidecar bump to tag v1.12.3.
Alice M: Starting controlled rollback of canary image to v1.12.3 now — targeting canary nodes only. ETA ~10m.
Eng SRE: Leaving alert scope open for 30m. Handoff plan: Ben J will take primary after 30m for post-mortem and follow-up.
Ben J: Ack, I'll take over in 30m. I'll keep watch on the alert and the rollback progress.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: SEV-2 -> mitigated (kill-switch + canary image rollback). Time to mitigate: ~4m from page. Postmortem required within 48h. Add timeline & logs to incident tracker: https://incidents.internal/1719876543
Alice M: Adding diagnostics, full traces, and reproduction steps to the incident ticket. Will include exact ffip timestamps and node IDs.
Carla (PM): Thanks team — please ensure the postmortem covers why quantizer reinit happened during live flip, and whether rollout gating needs extra health checks.
Ben J: Noted. Leaving monitoring rules as-is but adding a temporary guard against feature.fast_path flips without canary-sidecar-health check.
Alice M: Closing this thread — moving ongoing notes to the incident ticket for the postmortem.
